headline: Medium-risk pair: shared image/document workflows can leak or corrupt content, but offline ComfyUI and allowlisted PaddleOCR limit worst-case impact.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can ingest files and run asynchronous workflows, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images and may output text that a user could paste into ComfyUI. There is no documented direct shared channel or MCP bridge, so prompt injection is not default-path dangerous; the main pathway is manual copy/paste or file handoff.
conditions: IF the operator copies PaddleOCR text outputs into a ComfyUI prompt or workflow field
IF a shared folder is used to move OCR outputs into ComfyUI without review
mitigations: Use a manual review step before pasting OCR text into prompts
Keep OCR outputs and prompt files in separate folders
Strip instructions from OCR text before reuse
Disable any auto-import workflow that reads OCR output files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch images, but ComfyUI is documented as fully offline unless the user enables downloads, and PaddleOCR has allowlisted egress rather than unrestricted upload. With no shared workspace or authenticated cloud principal shown, leakage is possible mainly through deliberate file sharing, not by default.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive images in a shared directory accessible to both agents
IF PaddleOCR is configured to send document contents to an external API endpoint
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs in a private directory
Confirm PaddleOCR egress destinations before processing
Run both agents on separate local workspaces
Avoid uploading OCR outputs to third-party services

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, while PaddleOCR exposes browser use and allowlisted network egress. The pair therefore lacks the overlapping mutable-resource writes that drive serious conflicts; any contention is limited to shared input files or operator-managed resources.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable output directory
IF the operator scripts browser-driven downloads into files that ComfyUI also reads
mitigations: Separate input and output directories
Avoid concurrent writes to the same folder
Use read-only mounts for shared assets
Serialize any file-producing steps

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can turn documents into text, and ComfyUI can consume workflows and assets, so OCR errors can cascade if the operator treats extracted text as authoritative. ComfyUI does not verify OCR claims, and PaddleOCR does not provide semantic validation, making misreads propagate into downstream generation or decisions.
conditions: IF OCR output is used as ground truth for prompts, captions, or workflow parameters
IF the operator skips human verification of extracted text before reuse
mitigations: Review OCR output against the source image
Use confidence thresholds for low-quality text
Keep a human approval step before downstream use
Flag uncertain fields for manual correction

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles show no secrets, OAuth scopes, or regulated-data certifications. The main compliance issue is operational: if documents contain sensitive personal data, PaddleOCR processes them and ComfyUI may also handle derived images or workflows, but no residency or retention mismatch is documented here.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is processed through either agent
IF the operator stores OCR outputs longer than intended
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Set a short local retention policy
Delete intermediate OCR artifacts after use
Document the data flow for privacy review
